$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Fix this file, then regenerate. This is the third and last CONNECTOR piece of Tynn #9 (MOIC's meeting bot) -- Microsoft Graph's onlineMeeting resource, verified against Microsoft Learn's own reference pages on 2026-09-16 (application-post-onlinemeetings, onlinemeeting-get, onlinemeeting-list-transcripts). The BOT RUNTIME -- a service that actually joins a call and streams live media -- is the owner's call, not this estate's, and Graph's own path there is an application-hosted media bot: a .NET/Azure service, not a REST connector. What ships here: create a meeting (a join link), read it back, and find a finished meeting's transcript.
title: Microsoft Teams

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Replaced but NOT revoked -- the same Microsoft identity platform behaviour microsoft-outlook already documents: "Refresh tokens replace themselves with a fresh token upon every use. The Microsoft identity platform doesn't revoke old refresh tokens when used to fetch new access tokens." A retried or concurrent refresh cannot revoke the grant, which is the only thing the flag guards.
oauth.$scopeComment: OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite.All is what meeting_create and meeting_get need as APPLICATION permissions -- the /users/{userId}/onlineMeetings path a bot calls without a live user session, per Microsoft's own least-privilege table. OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All is what transcript_list needs. Both additionally require the tenant administrator's application access policy -- see the manifest's setup array, not just this comment, so the fact reaches a host through the registry index rather than only a reader of this file.
oauth.$comment: The package DECLARES the dance and does not perform it. `common` as the tenant accepts work, school and personal accounts, though the application-permission path this connector uses needs a WORK OR SCHOOL account specifically -- personal Microsoft accounts are not supported for any of these three operations, per Microsoft's own permission tables.

sandboxNote: Microsoft's test estate is a Microsoft 365 Developer Program sandbox: a separate E5 tenant with its own users and its own OAuth consent, on the SAME host -- the same fact microsoft-outlook already verified for Graph generally. Eligibility is limited (Visual Studio Professional/Enterprise, ISV Success / MAICPP partners, or Premier/Unified Support) and the tenant expires after 90 days of no development activity. Without one, every call reaches a real tenant.
summary: a Teams meeting or its transcripts, on behalf of a tenant user
$setupComment: The precondition every operation shares, moved out of oauth.$scopeComment and into a real setup step (2026-09-16, after Fancy pointed out that a $-prefixed key is commentary nothing downstream carries -- the registry index's entryFor() has no field for a host-actionable precondition, and would drop this exactly like idempotencyNote and the OAuth endpoints were once dropped). Verified against Microsoft Learn's own application-access-policy reference page.

setup.title: Register an app and add the OAuth redirect URL
setup.detail: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, App registrations, register (or reuse) an app and add {host.oauthRedirectUrl} under Authentication as a Web redirect URI. Record the Application (client) ID and create a client secret.

setup.title: Grant the app an application access policy naming the target user
setup.detail: OAuth consent alone does not authorize meeting_create, meeting_get or transcript_list -- Microsoft Graph refuses every call with "No application access policy found for this app" until a tenant administrator runs New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy (with this app's client ID) and Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy naming the userId these operations will act on. Changes take up to 30 minutes to reach the Graph REST API.

credentialFields.label: Application (client) ID
credentialFields.help: From the Microsoft Entra admin center -> App registrations. ONE value for the whole installation, not per connected account.

credentialFields.label: Client secret
credentialFields.help: A client secret of the same app registration. One value for the whole installation; Entra expires them, so record the expiry.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Microsoft account, and it expires after about ONE HOUR. The host refreshes it with the refresh token.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Per connected Microsoft account; issued only when the consent request includes offline_access. Every refresh answers with a NEW one -- persist it.
